# failover

```go
import "github.com/kinorai/omnifeed/internal/search/failover"
```

Package failover composes two domain.Searchers into one: a primary that answers every query, and a backup asked only when the primary's answer is an error, empty, thin, or degraded. The composite is itself a domain.Searcher, so a longer chain is nesting — failover\(a, failover\(b, c\)\) — and the transports never learn that more than one searcher exists.

The pieces are kept apart on purpose: Policy decides \(pure\), merge combines two rankings \(pure\), and Searcher only runs the two calls and reports what happened.

<a name="Action"></a>
## type Action

Action says what the composite does with the primary's answer.

```go
type Action int
```

<a name="Keep"></a>

```go
const (
    // Keep returns the primary's answer as is; the backup is not asked.
    Keep Action = iota
    // Replace answers with the backup alone: the primary has nothing worth
    // keeping.
    Replace
    // Merge answers with both, interleaved: the primary's results are real but
    // weaker than usual, and the backup tops them up.
    Merge
)
```

<a name="Config"></a>
## type Config

Config configures the Searcher.

```go
type Config struct {
    Primary domain.Searcher
    Backup  domain.Searcher
    Policy  Policy
    // PrimaryBudget, when > 0, bounds how long the primary may take before the
    // backup is asked instead. Without it a hung primary spends its whole
    // timeout-and-retry budget first (tens of seconds on SearXNG) and the
    // backup only starts after that. A primary cut off by the budget counts
    // as an error, so the backup replaces it.
    PrimaryBudget time.Duration
    Logger        *slog.Logger
    // Metrics, when non-nil, receives one omnifeed_search_fallbacks_total
    // increment per search handed to the backup.
    Metrics *observability.Metrics
}
```

<a name="Policy"></a>
## type Policy

Policy decides, from the primary's answer alone, whether the backup is worth asking. It is pure — no I/O, no clock — so every rule is a table test.

```go
type Policy struct {
    // MinResults is the result count below which a successful search counts as
    // thin and is topped up. 0 disables the thin trigger.
    MinResults int
}
```

<a name="Policy.Decide"></a>
### func \(Policy\) Decide

```go
func (p Policy) Decide(ctx context.Context, limit int, report domain.SearchReport, err error) Decision
```

Decide returns the action for the primary's \(report, err\) to a query that asked for at most limit results \(\<= 0: no limit\).

Two answers are never failed over. A caller that has gone away: the backup would answer nobody, and spend its own quota doing it. And a query refused for its input \(domain.ErrInvalidQuery\): the backup would refuse it too.

<a name="Searcher.Name"></a>
### func \(\*Searcher\) Name

```go
func (s *Searcher) Name() string
```

Name joins the members' names, e.g. "searxng\+tinyfish". It is the searcher label on omnifeed\_search\_requests\_total, so a dashboard can tell a deployment with a backup from one without. Computed once in New: transports read it on every search.

<a name="Searcher.Search"></a>
### func \(\*Searcher\) Search

```go
func (s *Searcher) Search(ctx context.Context, query string, opts domain.SearchOptions) (domain.SearchReport, error)
```

Search asks the primary, and the backup when the policy calls for it.

When the backup fails too, or replaces a failed primary with nothing, the primary's answer stands — its results if it had any, its error if not. The caller then sees the original failure, with its reason \(quota\_exhausted, timeout, ...\) intact: an empty success would read as "nothing exists" where the truth is "retry later".

<a name="Trigger"></a>
## type Trigger

Trigger names why the backup was asked.

```go
type Trigger string
```

<a name="TriggerError"></a>

```go
const (
    // TriggerError means the primary failed (pacing refused it, it timed out, the
    // upstream answered an error status, ...).
    TriggerError Trigger = "error"
    // TriggerEmpty means the primary succeeded with no results — on a pool of
    // engines that block silently, the shape of an outage.
    TriggerEmpty Trigger = "empty"
    // TriggerThin means the primary returned fewer results than Policy.MinResults.
    TriggerThin Trigger = "thin"
    // TriggerDegraded means the primary succeeded without a source it relies on
    // (domain.SearchReport.Degraded).
    TriggerDegraded Trigger = "degraded"
)
```
